other_errors_seen: hwloop-fuzz seeds 5050 and 5183 (with N/M/K from one.sh) produce wrong results on GVSoC vs the GAP9 GCC reference at O2, O3 and Os, with assembly identical between int-20 and F011, so the bug is pre-existing and not caused by this change. Both programs use hardware loops (lp.* count 6-8 and 1). Not investigated; possibly related to B03/B04. Reproduce with logs/20-F011.fuzz-one.sh <seed> from a copy of benchmarks/hwloop-fuzz.

The IR intrinsics llvm.riscv.pulp.clip/clipu and llvm.riscv.pulp.bextract[u] still accept inconsistent bounds or out-of-range values at the IR level (e.g. xpulpv.ll clip(-10,-4,15) encodes from Max only; clip with Max=INT_MAX gives immediate 32). This matters only for IR not produced by clang's builtins. Possible hardening: an IR verifier/ISel guard. Not in scope.
